scope: Exact resource owner/client authorization, separate routed registration provider, mandatory contract-local isolation, shared module client identity and registration-policy planning
commands: In simplepoint-react: pnpm i18n:sync; pnpm i18n:check; pnpm typecheck

distribution.probeOutput: Installed artifacts: isolated registration, separate provider, default-deny policy, unique planning class and two error locales verified

verifiedScenarios: Provider checks authenticated client_credentials identity and service-router.invoke against the exact configured resource owner before any domain mutation, including empty declarations
Missing policy/identity/scope, display-name impersonation, user credentials, mismatched owner and client are denied; binding freezes policy and rejects wildcard or malformed identities
Real signed JWT tests verify local service credentials, invalid signatures, grant type, scope, audience and revocation; caller browser/security/authorization context remains isolated
Missing local security contribution fails closed even when the caller has a valid service context
Consumer or provider contract can require local isolation regardless of the legacy host setting; a legacy consumer using a different Java interface still respects the provider requirement
Inbound JSON dispatcher uses the same policy and does not expose ResourceService management methods; explicit local plugin installation still reuses the domain implementation

Runtime credential configuration and registration policy planning use ModuleClientPlan; actual 20 domain modules plus workflow-http retain equal capabilities and resource-client policy across distributed, standalone and mixed deployment plans
Client identity planning rejects alias sharing across different hosts, including modules without resource declarations, and rejects overrides for unselected modules
Actual Common distribution uniquely packages the dedicated provider and identity planner, preserves isolation metadata, denies unconfigured registration and includes both error locales
limitations: Signed JWT and dispatcher verification is in-process; domain writes in security tests are explicit mocks, not a deployed OAuth/HTTP/browser acceptance
Policy generation is an API; actual credential provisioning, secret distribution, config publishing and cold-start/upgrade acceptance remain installer work
Legacy profile source mappings have not been applied to live Consul; modular hosts must use policies derived from their complete deployment plan
No persistent cross-process resource-catalog serialization, stale deployment generation fence, or automated legacy ownership adoption yet
No production data/config changes, deployment, commit or push; no temporary database or broker infrastructure was created in this increment
Standalone host, remaining HTTP/frontend contributions and three-topology end-to-end acceptance remain incomplete
